source_refs.note: OSWorld at 15 and 50 steps, averaged over 3 runs

expectations.applies_when: an empirical claim that a method improves end-to-end task success of a desktop (Ubuntu/Windows) computer-use agent
expectations.requirement: Report execution-checked success rate on OSWorld (or OSWorld-Verified) for desktop computer-use claims, stating the step budget (15 vs 50 steps) and observation setting

expectations.applies_when: an empirical claim that a method improves task success of an Android/mobile GUI agent
expectations.requirement: Report online success on AndroidWorld for mobile-agent claims, not only offline AndroidControl/AITW step metrics

source_refs.note: authors concede evaluation on 165-task WebArena-Lite subset due to cost

expectations.applies_when: an empirical claim that a training, data-synthesis or planning method improves a web agent on self-hosted sites
expectations.requirement: Report success on WebArena (self-hosted, functional-correctness checkers) for web-agent training or planning claims; if the 165-task WebArena-Lite or a per-template subset is used, say so and justify it

expectations.applies_when: a claim about web-agent success on real, live websites
expectations.requirement: Evaluate live-web agents on Online-Mind2Web (human-validated, start URL given, no search engine) or Mind2Web-Live rather than only WebVoyager, where a naive search-and-click agent already solves 51% of sampled tasks

source_refs.note: authors: ScreenSpot v1/v2 may not be robust enough to capture gains at scale

expectations.applies_when: a claim that a model or data recipe improves screenshot-to-coordinate GUI grounding
expectations.requirement: Report GUI grounding on ScreenSpot-Pro (high-resolution professional desktop) and ScreenSpot-v2, not only ScreenSpot v1, which saturates (7B and 72B indistinguishable)

expectations.applies_when: a claim that a grounding model or grounding-data recipe beats prior GUI grounders
expectations.requirement: Compare a new grounder against UGround(-V1-7B), Aguvis-7B/72B, OS-Atlas-7B and UI-TARS(-1.5) at matched backbone size

expectations.applies_when: a claim that a trained end-to-end GUI agent model improves online task success
expectations.requirement: Compare a native end-to-end GUI policy against UI-TARS(-1.5)-7B (or the same backbone's SFT-only model) and against an agentic framework (GPT-4o/o3 planner + specialised grounder such as UGround, Aria-UI, Jedi, GTA1)

expectations.applies_when: a claim that a grounding component (or the planner-grounder split itself) improves agent task success
expectations.requirement: For planner-grounder systems, hold the planner fixed and swap grounders (e.g. GPT-4o + UGround vs + Aguvis vs + Jedi), and report the planner alone

source_refs.note: vs SFT, Filtered BC, AWR, DigiRL

expectations.applies_when: a claim that an RL algorithm (online, offline-to-online, semi-online or model-based) improves a GUI/web agent
expectations.requirement: Compare GUI online-RL methods against DigiRL, WebRL, filtered BC / AWR and an SFT-only model trained on the same data

source_refs.note: agreement with human labels; held-out agents
authors concede VLM judges can admit failures or reject valid successes; no precision reported

expectations.applies_when: a method that uses an LLM/VLM judge, ORM or reflector to label trajectory success for evaluation, filtering or reward
expectations.requirement: Validate an LLM/VLM success judge or outcome reward model against human labels on trajectories from agents not used to build it (agreement/accuracy, plus the resulting success-rate gap)

source_refs.note: precision on AgentRewardBench; low recall noted
authors concede o4-mini WebJudge is overly conservative with low recall

expectations.applies_when: a claim that a GUI-agent judge, PRM or ORM is reliable enough to serve as reward or evaluator
expectations.requirement: Report judge reliability separately for positive and negative verdicts (precision and NPV, or precision/recall per class), not only overall accuracy

source_refs.note: authors: UPE not validated inside RL; abstention may bias kept samples
theory: systematic reward bias is not removed by more rollouts

expectations.applies_when: a claim that a learned reward model or verifier improves GUI-agent RL training

expectations.requirement: Measure execution checkers (evaluation scripts) two-sidedly: false negatives on alternative valid solutions as well as false positives

source_refs.note: authors: GPT-4o labels show significant gap to human experts

expectations.requirement: For PRMs or step-level verifiers, ablate the label source (human vs GPT-4o-generated step labels)

expectations.applies_when: a new benchmark or a claim about long-horizon GUI task capability
